display.purpose: Chapter titles and page-level headings in the reading experience. Always Crimson Pro.

headline.purpose: Section headings within the app. Crimson Pro for warmth.

title.purpose: Card titles, list items, sidebar sections. DM Sans for tool interface.

body.purpose: All UI text. DM Sans. Capped at 65ch for prose.

reading.purpose: Core reading experience. Literata with generous leading for multi-hour sessions.

label.purpose: Navigation, tabs, chapter numbers, form labels. Uppercase DM Sans.

mono.purpose: Code blocks in reader content, API keys. Fira Code.

shadows.name: resting
shadows.purpose: Cards at rest. Barely visible separation from background.

shadows.name: hover
shadows.purpose: Interactive cards on hover. Gentle lift.

shadows.name: elevated
shadows.purpose: Overlays and popovers above all content.

shadows.name: book
shadows.purpose: Physical book shadow. Multi-layer with inset bottom edge.

shadows.name: amber-glow

narrative.overview:
A favorite reading chair, afternoon light slanting through a window, a friend nearby who asks the right questions at the right time. That is the feeling read-pal's visual system aims to reproduce: unhurried warmth, the texture of paper and wood, the sense that knowledge lives here and someone cares about helping you find it.

The palette centers on Candlelight Gold (#d97706) as the single saturated accent against warm, paper-derived neutrals. Surfaces progress from cream to sandstone through four tonal tiers, creating depth without shadow. Typography shifts between two worlds: DM Sans handles the tool interface with calm efficiency, while Crimson Pro and Literata carry the reading experience with the warmth of well-set type.

This system explicitly rejects the generic SaaS dashboard and childish gamification. It is designed for people who read deeply and want to remember what they read.
keyCharacteristics: Warm, tonal surface layering over dramatic shadows
Single amber accent used sparingly (5-8% of any screen)
Dual typography registers: tool mode (sans) and reading mode (serif)
AAA contrast for body text in reading mode
Gently responsive interactions: unhurried transitions, warm hover states
Three reading themes (light, dark, sepia) that preserve warmth

rules.name: The Single Accent Rule
rules.body: Candlelight Gold is the only saturated color that appears as a painted element. Sage, Clay Red, and Pine Shadow are supporting voices for semantic meaning, never decoration.

rules.name: The Warm Neutral Rule
rules.body: Every gray in this system is tinted toward amber. Pure #808080, cool gray, or blue-gray is forbidden.

rules.name: The Dark Study Rule
rules.body: Dark mode is not inverted light mode. It is the same room after sunset: surfaces darken to deep navy-charcoal, text warms to parchment tones.

rules.name: The Two Register Rule
rules.body: Sans-serif is the tool interface. Serif is the reading experience. Never mix them within a single component.

rules.name: The Generous Leading Rule
rules.body: Reading mode line-height is 1.85, not the typical 1.5. This is a product where users read for 30-90 minutes.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Shadows appear only on reading-related elements or as a response to state (hover, focus, raised).

rules.name: The Warm Shadow Rule
rules.body: All shadow colors use rgba(30, 42, 56, ...) with warm-tinted navy, never pure black.

dos: Do use Candlelight Gold sparingly. More than 10% of a screen in amber means restraint is lost.
Do ensure 7:1 contrast ratio for all reading-mode body text (WCAG AAA).
Do use tonal surface layering for depth instead of shadows on non-reading elements.
Do respect the two-register typography rule: DM Sans for tools, Crimson Pro / Literata for reading.
Do use descriptive highlight colors that carry semantic meaning.
Do include focus-visible states on every interactive element.
Do animate with cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) for unhurried transitions.
donts: Don't use pure black (#000) or pure white (#fff). Every neutral must be tinted warm.
Don't create generic SaaS dashboard layouts with cold grays and blue accents (PRODUCT.md anti-reference).
Don't add playful gamification: stickers, mascots, confetti (PRODUCT.md anti-reference).
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with gradients).
Don't create hero-metric templates (big number, small label, gradient accent).
Don't build identical card grids. Vary sizes and layouts to reflect content hierarchy.
